doc.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

title: Lionel Hampton on breaking racial barriers
summary: Rowe relays Hampton's account of Teddy Wilson playing alone and of integrating the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Okay, we’ll proceed and it will go off in a while. You know who agrees with you about what you just said is Lionel Hampton. I had the pleasure of talking to him, God, like 25 years ago, and he said, Teddy Wilson used to play when Benny Goodman took an intermission and no white musician was on stage, then Teddy would play by himself. So I was the first one to break that tradition down. But the think about it, there was no black and white playing together no place. Not in moving pictures, not in baseball, football, no kind of sports.”
Yeah. Un hum. Yup. There you go.
